profile.beat: AI-economy growth equities: META's Muse agent, the neocloud and AI-power buildout, memory, AMD/NVDA, Rocket Lab and space, plus fintech (SOFI, HOOD) and occasional biotech and quantum news.
profile.style: Mostly news-and-analyst relay with a one-line interpretive kicker, mixed with 'who gets paid' stack lists. When personally committed, the author says so in portfolio terms: top position, sizing inside a family portfolio, LEAPS entries, or 'building the position before the revenue inflects'. The views are fundamental and narrative-led (TAM, moats, content per rack, cost of capital), with occasional valuation-multiple comparisons. Price-move posts ('absolutely flying right now') are frequent but carry no reasoning.
profile.cadence: High volume, often more than 30 posts a day: headline one-liners, 'Source:' follow-up replies, long stack threads, podcast and video promotion (Futurum Equities, THE DEEP DIVE / DEEP END), and casual replies to a small circle of fintwit accounts.
profile.revisits: Yes. META is revisited almost daily, from the moat framing (2100887511522496644) to the top-position claim (2102030053404230063) to a stated position size (2103117871278928350 thread, 2103118446464840151 reply). RKLB's full-stack thesis is restated repeatedly (2101816939761049805, 2102363716759249371, 2103157245496484253). Past calls are revisited as victory laps: P LEAPS (2103121045637238791) and VKTX LEAPS (2102361025542836625).
profile.caveats: The author runs a paid X subscription trading portfolio and promotes a podcast and a Futurum Equities affiliation, so the victory-lap posts about earlier LEAPS entries are self-promotional and not verifiable from this window. Most posts relay analyst notes or news, and those relays are not the author's own calls. Large, rising positions (META) are discussed with heavy after-the-fact confirmation bias. Risk is rarely addressed except for rates on SOFI and financing cost on the neoclouds.

narrative: The window is dominated by META. From 09-18 the author frames Muse's App Store rise as proof of Meta's installed-base moat, argues on 09-19 that the stock deserves a higher earnings multiple, and on 09-21 celebrates the rally as the payoff for buying fear, calling META the top family-portfolio position. Through Connect (09-23 to 09-24) they catalog every Muse partnership and hardware launch as evidence that Meta is becoming the consumer operating layer for AI. Alongside this runs a steady AI-infrastructure thread. Neoclouds (IREN, NBIS, CRWV) are called bullish, with the debate shifting on 09-21 toward cost of capital. Memory (MU, SKHY) is described as a tighter-for-longer cycle, and on 09-19 AMD is judged rich against NVDA before the author turns more constructive on AMD's agentic-CPU opportunity on 09-20. From 09-23 the emphasis moves to 'AI Power' as the next bottleneck: the author names VRT as a favorite and discloses adding heavily to ON on the drawdown. Rocket Lab's full-stack and Iridium story gets near-daily reinforcement. Rising Treasury yields and rate-hike odds appear as a headwind for SOFI and a puzzle given low VIX, but they do not change the growth-long posture.

picks.prospect: Muse turns Meta into the consumer operating layer for AI agents and drives a rerating of the stock beyond its ads business.
picks.risk_reward: The author notes Muse agentic calling is still early and wants retention or DAU data to confirm the habit forms, but otherwise frames the setup as asymmetric upside. No downside case is addressed.
picks.thesis: Meta's installed base lets a free product scale instantly. Muse adds connectors, payments (Shopify, PayPal, Meta Pay), glasses and dedicated hardware, and the transaction-fee model expands the TAM. The author built conviction before the narrative turned.

picks.thesis: Energized sites are the scarcest input, and lenders price that asset more cheaply than GPU-heavy balance sheets, which gives IREN the lowest cost of capital among the neoclouds.
